chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of those who narrated it, ascribing it upwards, saying:

If the alms-tax is prevented, the condition of the poor and the rich is worsened. I said: As for the poor, his condition is worsened because he is prevented from his right, but how is the condition of the rich worsened? He said: The rich who prevents (the deduction of) the alms-tax, his condition will worsen in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the rich when they withhold zakat?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the reciprocal spiritual and material dynamics of zakat, noting that while the poor suffer material deprivation, the rich incur spiritual loss in the Hereafter for withholding their obligatory dues. This narration underscores the concept of 'ta'abbud' (divine worship) in wealth purification, where the act of giving is as crucial for the giver's salvation as it is for the receiver's sustenance. It reflects the Shia emphasis on zakat as a mechanism for social equity and individual spiritual accountability.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Khalid, from some of what he narrated, that he ascribed it, saying:

If the alms tax is prevented, the condition of the poor and the rich is worsened. I said: As for the poor, his condition is worsened when he is prevented from his right, but how is the condition of the rich worsened? He said: The rich who prevents (the deduction of) the alms tax, his condition will worsen in the Hereafter.
